title: Fake Merc Character Study (part. 2): Section 308
summary: Part two of NH's character study of YouTuber Jason Blaha, presented as NH's own allegations and opinions. He covers alleged sock accounts, the Layne Norton harassment and lawsuit, bands and chains as artificial progression, suspected fake plates, inflated body fat claims, and diet flip-flops, and asks troll fans to stop egging him on.
claims: He says the subject raided his previous video with sock accounts, whose dislikes YouTube removed, and threatened a strike that cannot apply to a video of entirely original content
He claims to have identified about 75 sock accounts the subject uses to defend and compliment himself
He grew his own channel from zero using only YouTube comments
Most of a lolcow's followers are trolls who keep him going for entertainment, not genuine fans
Many fake-natty-exposing channels are driven by envy; exposing fakes is fine only when it protects young lifters

He recounts the Layne Norton affair as he understands it: the subject urged his community to harass Norton, whose pregnant wife received threats; he then lost the defamation case by not appearing and never apologized
Bands and chains can fake progression on camera: load goes up while raw strength stays flat; strength must be shown with straight weight
Accommodating resistance set up wrong, such as chains that never touch the floor, does nothing
He suspects the subject's plates are fake or mislabeled and would only believe the lifts if the plates were weighed on camera
A 5'7 lifter at 220 lb and 17% body fat would look like a tank; loose skin is an empty sack, so skin full of fat is just fat
He characterises the subject as a vulnerable narcissist who associates himself with high-status people to feel important
GOMAD (a gallon of milk a day) is idiotic even for people who need to gain weight; there are better calorie sources
Fans who fake-support the subject for laughs add to his misery; the goal is to make his followers realize their mistake
